# Getting started with mnemos-mesh

Build the binary, configure a two-node federation, run it, verify the
channel. This guide walks through a single node end-to-end; repeat the
peer-side steps on the remote node.

> **Audience:** operators setting up a federation peer. Assumes a
> running mnemos instance and Go 1.25+ installed.

---

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Go** | 1.25+ | Build the binary; pinned in `go.mod` |
| **mnemos** | v2.x | Local memory server; the mesh dials it over a Unix socket |
| **buf** | 1.72+ | Regenerate proto stubs (only if you edit `.proto` files) |
| **openssl** | any | Generate the private CA + node certs for mTLS |
| **golangci-lint** | v2.1+ | Lint gate in CI (`make lint`) |

All Go tools land in `~/go/bin/` — ensure it is on `$PATH`:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Korrnals/mnemos-mesh/blob/331ef3a785c1a74fb9f8972ff93cd6db5a8fc174/CONTRIBUTING.md) for install commands for
`buf` and the protoc generators.

---

## 1 · Build

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Korrnals/mnemos-mesh.git
cd mnemos-mesh
make build
./bin/mnemos-mesh version
```

The binary is static (`-trimpath -ldflags "-s -w"`), ~12MB. Cross-compile
for other targets with the CI commands — see
[`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/Korrnals/mnemos-mesh/blob/331ef3a785c1a74fb9f8972ff93cd6db5a8fc174/.github/workflows/ci.yml).

---

## 2 · Generate mTLS material

mnemos-mesh uses a **private CA** with mutual authentication and pinned
fingerprints (criterion 3). Generate the CA once per federation, and
one node cert per peer.

### Private CA (once, out-of-band)

```bash
openssl genrsa -out ca.key 4096
openssl req -x509 -new -key ca.key -sha256 -days 3650 \
  -subj "/CN=mnemos-mesh-ca" -out ca.pem
```

Keep `ca.key` offline. Distribute `ca.pem` to every node.

### Node cert (per node, CN = `node_id`)

```bash
# On node A
openssl genrsa -out node.key 2048
openssl req -new -key node.key -subj "/CN=mnemos-A" -out node.csr
openssl x509 -req -in node.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial \
  -days 365 -sha256 -out node.pem
```

Repeat on node B with `CN=mnemos-B`. The CN **must** match the
`node_id` in `mesh.yaml` — the mesh binds TLS identity to the peer id
used in ACL lookup and the `federation_access_log` (architecture §7).

### Compute the pinned fingerprint

```bash
openssl x509 -in node.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256
# sha256 Fingerprint=AB:CD:EF:...
```

Strip the `sha256 Fingerprint=` prefix and colons when entering it in
`mesh.yaml`; the loader accepts the `sha256:<hex>` form.

---

## 3 · Configure

Create `~/.mnemos/mesh.yaml`. See the
[configuration reference](mnemos-mesh/user/configuration) for every field,
and the [security model](mnemos-mesh/admin/security) for mTLS setup.

```yaml
node_id: mnemos-A
listen: 0.0.0.0:8443
unix_socket: /run/mnemos/core.sock

mtls:
  ca_cert: /etc/mnemos-mesh/ca.pem
  node_cert: /etc/mnemos-mesh/node.pem
  node_key: /etc/mnemos-mesh/node.key
  peer_fingerprints:
    mnemos-B: sha256:abcdef0123456789...
  rotation_days: 90

peers:
  - id: mnemos-B
    address: b.example.invalid:8443
    fingerprint: sha256:abcdef0123456789...
    projects: ["project-mnemos"]

mnemos:
  dial_timeout: 2s
  heartbeat_interval: 30s

logging:
  level: info
  format: json

metrics:
  listen: 127.0.0.1:9100
```

---

## 4 · Run

```bash
mnemos-mesh serve --config ~/.mnemos/mesh.yaml
```

The mesh opens the mTLS peer listener (`listen`) and dials mnemos
over the Unix socket (`unix_socket`). At M2 both halves are stubs:
every RPC returns `codes.Unimplemented`. Logic lands in M3 (Python
client) and beyond.

For production, run under systemd. A unit template is planned for M5
(production hardening); until then, run `mnemos-mesh serve` under a
process supervisor of your choice (systemd, supervisord, or an
init script).

---

## 5 · Connect mnemos (M3)

On the mnemos side, enable the MeshClient so mnemos dials
`/run/mnemos/core.sock`. The client lives in the mnemos repo
(`mnemos/src/mnemos/mesh_client.py`) and is delivered in M3. Until M3
ships, the mesh serves the peer listener but mnemos does not yet talk
to it.

---

<a id="verify"></a>

Once M3 lands, verify the channel with a heartbeat round-trip:

```bash
# On node A, with mnemos + mesh running
mnemos mesh heartbeat --peer mnemos-B
# Expected: a non-empty version field from the M2 binary
```

At M2 (stub), `mnemos-mesh doctor` is the verification tool — it
checks the Unix socket path, cert validity, and peer reachability
(stub). Run it after `serve`:

```bash
mnemos-mesh doctor --config ~/.mnemos/mesh.yaml
```

---

## Troubleshooting

### Unix socket not found

```text
config: read /run/mnemos/core.sock: no such file or directory
```

The mesh creates the socket; mnemos dials it. Ensure the directory
exists and the mnemos process has not already bound a different path.
Check `unix_socket` in both configs matches.

### mTLS rejection — unknown peer

```text
mtls: peer fingerprint not in pinned set
```

The connecting peer's cert fingerprint is not in
`mtls.peer_fingerprints`. Add it (computed in step 2) or verify the
peer is presenting the expected cert. A peer whose CN does not match
a pinned id is rejected before any RPC is dispatched.

### mTLS rejection — CA validation failed

```text
tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

The peer's cert does not chain to the configured `ca_cert`. Ensure
every node uses certs signed by the same private CA, and that
`ca_cert` points at the right `ca.pem`.

### Config parse error

```text
config: parse ~/.mnemos/mesh.yaml: yaml: ...
```

A YAML syntax error. Validate the file with `yq` or `python -c
"import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('mesh.yaml'))"`. Common causes: a
fingerprint with colons (strip them or use the `sha256:<hex>` form),
or a missing `node_id` (required — binds the mTLS cert CN).

### `node_id must not be empty`

`node_id` is required. It binds to the mTLS cert CN (criterion 3,
architecture §7) and is used as the peer id in ACL lookup and the
`federation_access_log`. Set it to match the cert CN.
